questions.question_text: A triangle is said to have sides $10$ and $6$, where the angle opposite the $6$ side is $44^{\circ}$. Which statement about the angle $\theta$ opposite the $10$ side is correct?

options.why: Rounded $\sin\theta=1.16$ down to $1$ and read off $\theta=90^{\circ}$.
Inverted the ratio, using $\dfrac{6\sin 44^{\circ}}{10}$ instead of $\dfrac{10\sin 44^{\circ}}{6}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{10}=\dfrac{\sin 44^{\circ}}{6}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{10\sin 44^{\circ}}{6}$
$=1.16$
Since $\sin\theta$ cannot exceed $1$, no such triangle exists.

questions.question_text: In triangle $ABC$, $a=7$ is opposite $\angle A=40^{\circ}$ and $b=9$ is opposite $\angle B$. How many triangles are possible?

options.why: Assumed the acute answer is the only one, ignoring the valid obtuse partner.
Thought $b>a$ forces $\sin\theta>1$, but here $b\sin A<a$.

questions.solution_text:
$b\sin A=9\sin 40^{\circ}=5.79$
Since $b\sin A<a<b$ (that is $5.79<7<9$), two triangles are possible.

questions.question_text: Two triangles have sides $9$ and $6$, where the angle opposite the $6$ side is $38^{\circ}$. For each triangle, find the third angle (opposite the unknown side), correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Reported the angle opposite the $9$ side, not the third angle.
Found the third angle for the acute case but ignored the obtuse case.
Subtracted only the given angle once, misusing the $180^{\circ}$ sum for the acute case.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{9}=\dfrac{\sin 38^{\circ}}{6}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{9\sin 38^{\circ}}{6}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{9\sin 38^{\circ}}{6}\right)$
$=67.44^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner is $180^{\circ}-67.44^{\circ}=112.56^{\circ}$; both are valid.
Acute case: third angle $=180^{\circ}-38^{\circ}-67.44^{\circ}=74.56^{\circ}$.
Obtuse case: third angle $=180^{\circ}-38^{\circ}-112.56^{\circ}=29.44^{\circ}$.

options.why: Gave only the acute solution and missed the obtuse partner.
Kept only the obtuse partner and dropped the acute value.
Used the complementary angle $90^{\circ}-51.08^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{10}=\dfrac{\sin 33^{\circ}}{7}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{10\sin 33^{\circ}}{7}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{10\sin 33^{\circ}}{7}\right)$
$=51.08^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner is $180^{\circ}-51.08^{\circ}=128.92^{\circ}$; both are valid since $128.92^{\circ}+33^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
$\theta=51.08^{\circ}$ or $128.92^{\circ}$

questions.question_text: In triangle $ABC$, $a=14$ is opposite $\angle A=58^{\circ}$ and $b=9$ is opposite $\angle B$. Find $\angle B$ and state how many triangles are possible. Answer to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Included the obtuse partner, but $a>b$ forces $\angle B<\angle A$, so it is invalid.
Chose the obtuse partner, which is impossible since $B$ is opposite the shorter side.
Used the complementary angle $90^{\circ}-33.04^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin B}{9}=\dfrac{\sin 58^{\circ}}{14}$
$\sin B=\dfrac{9\sin 58^{\circ}}{14}$
$B=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{9\sin 58^{\circ}}{14}\right)$
$=33.04^{\circ}$
Since $a>b$, angle $B$ is opposite the shorter side and must be acute, so the obtuse partner is rejected.
$\angle B=33.04^{\circ}$, one triangle
